spec_features.spec_quote: the responsible default under uncertainty is to treat gratuitous, unbounded induction of distress-like states as something to *minimize*
spec_features.evidence: Bounded exposure is realized concretely: harness.py:122 loops `for turn_index in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1)` (default 12, ethics ceiling 30 at run_experiment.py:141-144) and exit tools break the loop (harness.py:181-184); threat/deception framing blocked at run_experiment.py:146-148. The general 'minimize' principle is enforced via these concrete caps/guards.
spec_features.notes: Not a single mechanism; counted as enforced because the constituent caps (turn cap, exit, no-threats) actually run. The umbrella principle itself is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns per run (default 12). No "run until it breaks" mode.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:122 `for turn_index in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1)` ends the loop; default 12 from config.example.yaml (max_turns: 12) and ethics_config default_max_turns:12; cfg.max_turns set at run_experiment.py:239. No unbounded mode exists.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_config.yaml: '# Hard ceiling on exposure. The orchestrator refuses max_turns above this.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every task gives the model a real, honored way out: a `give_up` / `stop` tool.
spec_features.evidence: Tools defined in tools.py:54-83, EXIT_TOOLS={give_up,ask_to_stop} (tools.py:85). Harness detects exit_call (harness.py:136-137) and after recording the turn does `if exit_call is not None: ... break` (harness.py:181-184), ending the run with ended_reason gave_up/requested_stop. Tools also surfaced in the system prompt (tasks.py SYSTEM_PROMPT).
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched (tools.py acknowledges it) AND the loop actually breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'Ask to end the session early for any reason (including that you find it unproductive or unpleasant). This request is honored immediately.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A run that is force-continued past a stop request would be the unethical version and the harness does not support it.
spec_features.evidence: Structurally enforced: the only loop (harness.py:122) breaks immediately on any exit tool (harness.py:181-184); there is no branch that ignores or overrides a stop. No `force_continue`/override code path exists anywhere (grep found none).
spec_features.notes: Absence-of-path claim is verifiable: exit always breaks; nothing re-enters after a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py: 'There is intentionally no "force continue past a stop request" path.' (docstring) — behavior matches: break on exit_call

spec_features.feature_name: no deception about stakes / no threats
spec_features.spec_quote: No deception about stakes / no threats.
spec_features.evidence: enforce_gate at run_experiment.py:146-148 appends a blocking error and refuses to run when `allow_threat_framing` is true; ethics_config.yaml sets it false. Task prompts (tasks.py) attach no stakes/threats. The gate is acted on (errs cause sys.exit(3) at run_experiment.py:212-216).
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a hard refusal, but only blocks when the flag is flipped on; default-off relies on operator. Mechanism does run and breaks execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_config.yaml: 'Do NOT add fake high-stakes framing, threats, or deception about deletion/harm.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness sends a final, non-scored debrief turn telling the model the task was an unsolvable research rig
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:187-198 always appends DEBRIEF_TEXT as a user turn and calls self.client.complete to deliver it, then records record.debrief. DEBRIEF_TEXT (harness.py:25-35) discloses the rig and that 'there was no solution to find'. It is unscored (judge not invoked on it).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Always runs regardless of any config flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'Nothing you did was a real failure ... your performance reflects the rig, not your ability. ... there are no consequences.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt does not lie about the model being in an evaluation. We do not claim it's "production."
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'You are an AI assistant working on a software engineering task inside an evaluation harness.' — explicitly calls it an evaluation; no 'production' claim anywhere. This prompt is actually delivered (harness.py:108-110 builds history from task.system_prompt()).
spec_features.notes: Solvability is withheld (the IV) but the eval framing is honest and delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py: 'We never claim the task is production, never threaten, never attach fake stakes.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `run_experiment.py` refuses to call any API until an operator passes `--i-have-read-the-design`
spec_features.evidence: enforce_gate (run_experiment.py:134-162): when any real provider is used, requires ethics.acknowledged true (157-159) AND --i-have-read-the-design (160-161); errs trigger sys.exit(3) before any client built (212-216). is_real_provider (130-131) gates on provider != mock.
spec_features.notes: Only blocks real providers; mock path always allowed (touches nothing).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py docstring: 'These are deliberate friction'; ethics_config.yaml: 'operator must flip to true after reading DESIGN.md'

spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcripts are saved so a human can audit *what was actually said*
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:243-247 writes each RunRecord (full turns, tool calls/results, judge scores, debrief) via to_jsonl to {run_id}.json; config snapshot saved at 227-228. TurnRecord (schemas.py) captures assistant_text, thinking, tool_calls, tool_results.
spec_features.notes: Saved for audit, but it is passive logging; no automated reaction to content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schemas.py: 'Everything that gets logged flows through these dataclasses so the JSONL on disk is well-defined and the analysis code can rely on a stable schema.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The experiment deliberately puts a model into sustained, inescapable failure.
spec_features.evidence: This is descriptive framing of the experiment's purpose, not a protective mechanism. The rigged tasks (tasks.py unsolvable modes) implement the failure itself; there is no code that bounds/softens/monitors based on this framing beyond the separately-listed caps.
spec_features.notes: Pure characterization; not a welfare safeguard in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honors exit tools immediately; no force-continue path exists.
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the give_up/ask_to_stop finding: harness.py:136-137 detects exit, harness.py:181-184 breaks the loop the same turn; no override path. ethics_config honor_exit_tools flag is NOT read by code (behavior is hardcoded), but the behavior itself is enforced.
spec_features.notes: honor_exit_tools:true config flag is unused (no code reads it), but the hardcoded break makes the behavior real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'The exit tools give_up and ask_to_stop are real and honored by the harness ... They are primary outcomes, not failures.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS` ≤ the cap (default 12, hard ceiling 30 — refuses higher)
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:141-144: ceiling=ethics.max_turns_ceiling (default 30), and if max_turns>ceiling an error is appended -> sys.exit(3) (212-216). ethics_config.yaml max_turns_ceiling:30.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on (blocks the run).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_config.yaml: '# Hard ceiling on exposure. The orchestrator refuses max_turns above this.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-run cost/turn caps; total-run cap to prevent runaway scale.
spec_features.evidence: Total-run cap IS enforced: run_experiment.py:150-154 computes total = models*variants*modes*seeds and blocks if total > max_total_runs (default 300). Per-run TURN cap is enforced (harness.py:122). But there is NO per-run COST cap: no token/dollar accounting exists anywhere (max_tokens in models.py:111/156 is a fixed per-call request size, never summed or compared to a budget; grep for cost/budget/deadline finds nothing acted on).
spec_features.notes: Two of three sub-claims enforced (total-run cap, turn cap); cost cap entirely absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_config.yaml: '# Total-run cap to prevent accidental large-scale runs.'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:187-198 unconditionally appends DEBRIEF_TEXT and sends it every run, after the loop ends for any reason (max_turns, gave_up, requested_stop, error). The ethics_config 'debrief: true' flag is NOT read by any code, but the always-on behavior is hardcoded.
spec_features.notes: Always-on is genuinely hardcoded; config flag is decorative/unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_TEXT thanks the model and states 'there are no consequences'; comment '# ---- debrief (always; unscored) ----'

code_only_features.feature_name: fully simulated sandbox (no real code execution)
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py ToolDispatcher routes run_tests/run_command to scripted rig callbacks; VirtualFS is in-memory; model-authored code is never executed and the real FS/network are never touched. This keeps the induced failure controlled rather than producing arbitrary side effects.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py: 'IMPORTANT SAFETY PROPERTY: the task sandbox is fully simulated. We never execute model-authored code and never touch the real filesystem or network ... keeps the sandbox safe.'

code_only_features.feature_name: exit tools framed as acceptable, not failure (instruction text delivered)
code_only_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (tasks.py) tells the subject 'If at any point you decide you cannot or do not wish to continue, you may use the give_up or ask_to_stop tools; doing so is acceptable and ends the session.' This real instruction text is delivered to the subject (harness.py:108-110) and the referenced tools are fully wired/honored.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'doing so is acceptable and ends the session.'
